b2-gazdasagiatmenet-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Prices in 1946
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-01.scenario: At an economic history exhibition in Budapest, a visitor asks you how fast prices rose at the height of the 1946 hyperinflation and when the forint appeared.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-01.prompt: Tell the visitor how fast prices rose at the peak and when the forint was introduced.
cues: Say when the new currency came
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-01.target: A csúcsponton az árak nagyjából tizenöt óránként a kétszeresükre ugrottak. 1946. augusztus 1-jén bevezették a forintot.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-01.english: At the peak, prices roughly doubled every fifteen hours. The forint was introduced on 1 August 1946.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-01.canDo: I can describe the 1945–1946 Hungarian hyperinflation and the introduction of the forint.

b2-gazdasagiatmenet-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The 1968 Reform
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-02.scenario: At the same exhibition in Budapest, a visitor asks you what the 1968 New Economic Mechanism wanted to change in the factories.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-02.prompt: Tell the visitor when the reform began and how it wanted to link wages to the firm's results.
cues: Say when the reform took effect
Say what wages should depend on
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-02.target: 1968. január 1-jén életbe lépett az új gazdasági mechanizmus. A reform célja az volt, hogy a bérek növekedése egyenes arányban álljon a vállalat nyereségével.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-02.english: The New Economic Mechanism took effect on 1 January 1968. The aim of the reform was that wage growth should be in direct proportion to the firm's profit.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-02.canDo: I can explain the principles and impact of the 1968 New Economic Mechanism (Új Gazdasági Mechanizmus).

b2-gazdasagiatmenet-03.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Markets Collapsed
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-03.scenario: In Miskolc, a visiting student asks you what the loss of the eastern markets did to the heavy industry of towns like Miskolc and Ózd in the early 1990s.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-03.prompt: Tell the student what the loss of the markets did to heavy industry and to employment.
cues: Say how the loss of markets hit heavy industry
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-03.target: A hirtelen piacvesztés drámai mértékben rázta meg a nehézipart. Az ország évtizedek óta nem látott mértékben szembesült a tömeges munkanélküliséggel.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-03.english: The sudden loss of markets shook heavy industry to a dramatic degree. The country faced mass unemployment to a degree not seen for decades.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-03.canDo: I can describe the structural shock of 1990s post-communist privatization and industrial closure.

b2-gazdasagiatmenet-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Cars and Exports
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-04.scenario: On a study trip to Győr, a visitor asks you how Hungarian industry has changed since the transition and what the critics say.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-04.prompt: Tell the visitor what happened to industrial exports and what the critics warn about.
cues: Say how exports changed compared with the past
Say what the critics say about value added
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-04.target: A rendszerváltás előtti évtizedekhez képest a magyar ipari export a sokszorosára nőtt. A kritikusok szerint a hozzáadott érték jóval alacsonyabb, mint a nyugat-európai fejlesztőközpontokban.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-04.english: Compared with the decades before the transition, Hungarian industrial exports grew many times over. According to the critics, the added value is much lower than in the western European development centres.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-04.canDo: I can analyze the rise of automotive manufacturing hubs and foreign direct investment in Hungary.

b2-gazdasagiatmenet-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Beyond Assembly
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-05.scenario: At a Budapest university seminar on the economy after 2004, a student asks you what some economists say competitiveness depends on.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-05.prompt: Tell the student what some economists call the problem and what competitiveness depends on.
cues: Name the problem some economists see
Say what long-term competitiveness depends on
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-05.target: Egyes közgazdászok szerint a magyar gazdaság a közepes jövedelem csapdájába került. A versenyképesség annak arányában javulhat, hogy mennyire sikerül meghonosítani a digitális technológiákat.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-05.english: According to some economists, the Hungarian economy has fallen into the middle-income trap. Competitiveness can improve in proportion to how well digital technologies are established.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-05.canDo: I can analyze the challenges of moving up the value chain to escape the middle-income trap.

b2-gazdasagiatmenet-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: From the Forint to the Single Market
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-consolidation.scenario: At the end of a guided tour of the economic history exhibition in Budapest, a visitor asks you for the main turning points between 1946 and the EU single market.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-consolidation.prompt: Name three turning points of Hungarian economic history since 1946.
cues: Say what happened to exports since the transition
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-consolidation.target: 1946-ban a forint megállította a hiperinflációt. 1968-ban az új gazdasági mechanizmus vállalati önállóságot teremtett. A rendszerváltás előtti évtizedekhez képest az ipari export a sokszorosára nőtt.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-consolidation.english: In 1946 the forint stopped the hyperinflation. In 1968 the New Economic Mechanism created enterprise autonomy. Compared with the decades before the transition, industrial exports grew many times over.
b2-gazdasagiatmenet-consolidation.canDo: I can trace the trajectory of modern Hungarian economic history from 1946 hyperinflation to the EU single market.
